clues: This town is an oasis at the north edge of the Sahara Desert in Algeria. It sits in dry hills far south of the capital, Algiers.
Some years bring harsh drought, with very little rain at all. Then sand dunes creep in from the north, and a green belt of gardens helps hold them back.
In 1852 French troops laid a brutal siege to this town. After it fell, the town stayed under French rule for more than a hundred years.
Not far from town lies a huge store of natural gas under the ground. It is the second largest store of its kind in all of Africa.
If you see fine rugs and bright cloth hangings woven by hand, think of this market town. That craft is what it is most known for.
